home.subtitle: Fullstack Developer & Systems Administrator
home.description: Hello, I'm Marcos Reyes, a Fullstack Developer and Systems Administrator. I build user-friendly apps and solve tech problems using modern tools. I enjoy learning new things and keeping up with industry trends. Let's connect and work together!
home.whoami_text: I am a passionate Fullstack Developer and Systems Administrator with experience in building web applications and managing technological infrastructures. I specialize in creating efficient and scalable solutions that meet end-user needs. My focus is on code quality, performance optimization, and security. I am always looking to learn new technologies and improve my skills to deliver the best in every project I work on.

tech-stack.title: Tech Stack
tech-stack.description: Throughout my journey as a developer, I've had the opportunity to work with a wide variety of technologies and tools. Some might say I have quite the attention deficit for learning so many things, but I believe there's nothing wrong with adapting to different stacks beyond your own. Of course, I have my favorites. Below you'll find a summary of the technologies I feel most comfortable working with and use most frequently in my projects.

gallery.title: My Gallery
gallery.description: Welcome to my personal collection of pictures that inspire me and shows my journey through this life.

IMG_2741.title: Playing Touhou on my ThinkPad with Wine
IMG_2741.description: A photo of a ThinkPad laptop displaying a Touhou game, running on Wine. While I was using Arch Linux on my ThinkPad, I decided to play some Touhou games using Wine.

IMG_1981.title: Coding in the truck in the middle of traffic
IMG_1981.description: After a day of traveling, my mother picked me up in her truck. While we were stuck in traffic, I took the opportunity to code on my laptop. Time is gold!

IMG_3309.title: Coding in my yard while my cat watches me
IMG_3309.description: On a spring day, I decided to code in my yard while my cat, Agustin, was nearby watching me. Drinking Pepsi, by the way!

IMG_3642.title: Monster Mango Loco while waiting for car service
IMG_3642.description: Enjoying a Monster Mango Loco drink while waiting for my car to be serviced.

IMG_2967.title: My first Raspberry Pi Zero 2W.
IMG_2967.description: That day I received my first Raspberry Pi Zero 2W. I was really incredulous because I thought all Raspberry Pis (and their cases) used screws to secure them, but since the Pi Zero 2W is smaller, almost like a USB drive, just a little bigger, it just clicked into place and stayed put. I thought the seller had ripped me off or something, lol.

IMG_4023.title: SOCOM 3 U.S. Navy SEALs multiplayer on PS2 (PCSX2)
IMG_4023.description: That was so fun! I never thought I would play SOCOM 3 U.S. Navy SEALs multiplayer again after so many years. Thanks to PCSX2, I could relive those moments playing with friends online. In 4K too!

IMG_2422.title: Booting my Raspberry Pi 4B
IMG_2422.description: I just installed Raspbian on my Raspberry Pi 4B and I'm booting it up for the first time. Excited to explore all the projects I can do with it!

IMG_3596.title: Playing Halo Infinite Campaign on my OMEN 16
IMG_3596.description: I never used this laptop for gaming; I bought it for my programming career. After I finished my studies, I reinstalled Windows and started using it for video games. Halo Infinite looks amazing on it!

IMG_4122.title: Weather forecast with Arduino Uno, I2C LCD, and DHT11
IMG_4122.description: I really love I2C; it's so easy to use and saves a lot of pins on the Arduino. In this project, I used an Arduino Uno, my 'Jenny' board—a custom Arduino Uno with waifu graphics, integrated buzzer, lights showing what pins are being used in real time, and a lot of details. The project shows the temperature and humidity using a DHT11 sensor and an I2C LCD display.

IMG_4135.title: The same I2C LCD weather forecast project but with an ESP8266
IMG_4135.description: I recreated the weather forecast project using an ESP8266 instead of an Arduino Uno. The ESP8266 allows for Wi-Fi connectivity, so I added features to fetch weather data from the internet and display it on the I2C LCD. Personally, I prefer using the ESP8266 over the ESP32 for simpler projects.

IMG_4227.title: My Degree Certificate
IMG_4227.description: After 3 years of hard work (and dealing with uncooperative people), I finally graduated as a Computer Programming Analyst from Duoc UC institute. This certificate gives me a lot to think about. It's not that it excites me or matters too much, but in the early semesters I had pretty average grades and uncommitted teams, to be honest. However, in the last semesters I became more self-sufficient and had better teams, managing to pass with the highest grades, literally. Interestingly, my first grade in the program was a 1.0 due to an anxiety attack, and my final portfolio grade was a 7.0, the highest grade in Chile.
